events.title: .NET Framework 2.0 and C# 2.0 released
events.summary: Microsoft shipped .NET Framework 2.0 on November 7, 2005 with C# 2.0 generics, nullable types, partial classes, and iterators.
events.about: C# 2.0 generics brought `List<T>` and type-safe collections to the CLR — matching Java 5's headline feature on Microsoft's stack. Nullable value types, `yield return`, and anonymous methods paved the way for LINQ in C# 3. WinForms and ASP.NET 2.0 shipped alongside for enterprise Windows development.

narrative.whyChosen: C# 2.0 generics made .NET a credible enterprise language alongside Java.
narrative.whyImportant: Generics and iterators were prerequisites for LINQ and modern C# frameworks.
narrative.problemSolved: C# 1.0 boxed everything as `object`; developers needed type-safe collections and cleaner iteration.

events.title: Firefox 1.5 released
events.summary: Mozilla shipped Firefox 1.5 on November 29, 2005 with faster back/forward navigation, drag-and-drop tabs, and live bookmarks.
events.about: Firefox 1.5 refined the browser that had broken IE's monopoly: incremental speed gains, better RSS integration, and smoother tab dragging kept users from returning to Internet Explorer. It maintained Mozilla's momentum through the mid-2000s browser wars.

narrative.whyChosen: Firefox 1.5 sustained the post-1.0 growth that made Mozilla a permanent browser player.
narrative.whyImportant: Performance and UX polish proved Firefox was not a one-release wonder.
narrative.problemSolved: Early Firefox needed faster navigation and tab management to match user expectations set by IE.
